title: Renewable-compatible urea electrosynthesis enabled by dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains
abstract:
Fluctuating renewable electricity challenges selective urea electrosynthesis because catalysts often operate within narrow potential windows. Here, the authors design dynamic asymmetric copper–rhodium catalytic domains that buffer charge and sustain urea production under variable electrical input. 
 Electrocatalytic C–N coupling offers a sustainable route to produce urea from CO2 and nitrate, yet most catalysts operate within narrow potential windows, limiting their performance under fluctuating renewable power. Here we show that dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains composed of Cu single-atoms (CuSA) and Cu-Rh single-atom alloys (Cu1RhSAA), in which asymmetric sites are bridged by an elastic Cu/Rh–O–V electronic bridge. These two Cu environments promote initial C–N coupling and subsequent hydrogenation, respectively, while the elastic electronic bridges redistribute excess charge and help preserve the local coordination environment as the potential changes. This design achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency (FE) > 65% from −0.2 to −0.6 V and reaches a yield rate of 234.39 mmol h−1 g−1. Under a seven-day variable-potential protocol informed by solar irradiance, the mean urea FE is 70.0 ± 8.0%. Techno-economic and life-cycle assessments indicate favorable environmental and economic potential. These results establish dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains as a general strategy for scalable, renewable-compatible electrosynthesis of nitrogen-containing products. Fluctuating renewable electricity challenges selective urea electrosynthesis because catalysts often operate within narrow potential windows. Here, the authors design dynamic asymmetric copper–rhodium catalytic domains that buffer charge and sustain urea production under variable electrical input.

title: Canadian lakes show contrasting phosphorus trends across climatic regions
abstract:
Lake phosphorus increased in Arctic Canada but declined across other climatic regions, with northern increases linked to ground warming and soil erosion, according to a study that combined field measurements with deep learning analysis of Landsat imagery from 15,240 lakes between 1984 and 2025. 
 Phosphorus regulates lake productivity and water quality, yet long-term changes in lake phosphorus and their climatic drivers remain poorly understood at continental scales. Here we show how total phosphorus changes across 15,240 Canadian lakes > 5 km2 from 1984 to 2025 using a deep neural network trained with 35,452 field measurements and applied to 386,727 Landsat images. Arctic tundra watersheds show increasing phosphorus concentrations of 0.15 μg/L yr−1, whereas boreal forest, temperate forest, agricultural and urban watersheds show declines of 0.07, 0.11, 0.16 and 0.12 μg/L yr−1, respectively. Path analyses link northern increases to ground warming and soil erosion, consistent with permafrost-related phosphorus mobilization. Southern declines are associated with vegetation greening, hydrological change, and reduced human phosphorus inputs, while surface runoff remains important in agricultural and urban systems. These findings reveal contrasting climate-sensitive phosphorus trajectories and show that climate change can reinforce or counteract nutrient management gains, highlighting the need to integrate region-specific climate adaptation into lake management. title: Regionalized greenhouse gas emissions and infrastructure requirements for future global iron and steel production
abstract:
Global steel production emits about 3.7 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent annually and could be cut by up to 70% by 2040, but would require vast hydrogen, carbon storage, and electricity infrastructure, according to a global life cycle assessment and scenario analysis. 
 The steel industry accounts for approximately 7–9% of global greenhouse gas emissions, making it a key sector for decarbonization. Here, we quantify current and prospective greenhouse gas emissions from crude steel production facilities worldwide. Based on life cycle assessment, current greenhouse gas emissions of global crude steel production are around 3.7 gigatonnes carbon dioxide equivalent per year, highly concentrated in Asia. Depending on the future 2◦C scenario in 2040, greenhouse gas emissions may decline by up to 70%, to 1.1–2.3 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent per year. Also, we show that decarbonizing steel may require up to 90 million tonnes of hydrogen per year, 1.0 gigatonne of carbon dioxide storage per year, and/or electricity supply with up to 6,000 terawatt-hours per year, more than twice the European Union’s current electricity supply. Our results highlight the importance of regional context and the substantial infrastructure needs of low-carbon steel production. title: Effusive sedimentary volcanism experimentally reproduced under Martian-like conditions
abstract:
Depressurization-induced boiling sustains rather than quenches low-pressure sedimentary eruptions, driving eruptive transport and surface emplacement and providing new insights into mud volcanism on Mars and other planetary bodies, according to experimental, numerical, and thermal modeling analyses. 
 Rapid boiling, cooling, and freezing are commonly assumed to rapidly quench metastable liquid eruptions exposed to near-vacuum planetary environments, influencing both sedimentary volcanism on Mars and cryovolcanism on icy worlds. However, how these coupled phase transitions govern eruptive processes remains largely unknown. Here we show experimentally that boiling instead sustains coupled ballistic-effusive mud eruptions under Martian-like pressure conditions (~4.5 mbar). Using an ice-sealed metastable reservoir, we reproduced subsurface-driven eruptions initiated by internally generated boiling-induced overpressure. Eruptions evolved systematically from short-lived ballistic fountains toward episodic effusive emplacement accompanied by coherent mud-flow formation. Ballistic transport redistributed liquid mud around the vent and promoted proximal accumulation that subsequently coalesced into sustained flows despite ongoing cooling and freezing. Numerical modeling further demonstrates that erupted mud would remain largely unfrozen during ballistic transport under Martian gravity conditions. Together, our results show that rapid boiling does not suppress sedimentary volcanism under low-pressure conditions, but instead actively sustains eruptive transport and surface emplacement. These findings provide new constraints on this process on Mars and establish a broader physical framework for metastable liquid eruptions across the Solar System. Depressurization-induced boiling sustains rather than quenches low-pressure sedimentary eruptions, driving eruptive transport and surface emplacement and providing new insights into mud volcanism on Mars and other planetary bodies, according to experimental, numerical, and thermal modeling analyses.

title: Warming since the Last Glacial Maximum amplifies Northern Hemisphere drought expansion driven by the Pacific Decadal Oscillation
abstract:
The Pacific Decadal Oscillation regime shifts modulate the spring precipitation patterns across East Asia and western North America by altering subtropical trough positions, and the drying effect associated with its negative phase is amplified by warming since the Last Glacial Maximum, as revealed by reanalysis and model experiments. 
 The Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) modulates decadal precipitation patterns, and subtropical troughs act as rainfall “commanders”. However, whether PDO influences precipitation variability by affecting these troughs remains unclear. By combining reanalysis data with present-day and Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) simulations, we reveal that PDO regime shifts regulate spring precipitation by altering subtropical trough positions and associated wind patterns. A negative PDO phase deepens the India-Burma trough and shifts its base ~1330 km equatorward, inducing northeasterly anomalies to its east that weaken moisture transport and suppress precipitation over East Asia. Concurrently, it shallows the North American subtropical trough and shifts its base ~560 km poleward, promoting a ridge development that reduces precipitation in water-stressed western North America. Notably, the 4-6 °C warming since the LGM has amplified the negative PDO drying effect, increasing affected area by 160% in East Asia and 57% in North America. These results clarify how the PDO regulates subtropical trough dynamics to shape spring precipitation, providing a mechanistic basis for drought risk assessments under similar warming magnitude to that projected for this century. The Pacific Decadal Oscillation regime shifts modulate the spring precipitation patterns across East Asia and western North America by altering subtropical trough positions, and the drying effect associated with its negative phase is amplified by warming since the Last Glacial Maximum, as revealed by reanalysis and model experiments.

title: Free tropospheric halogen oxidation drives mercury deposition in the Asia Pacific region
abstract:
Free tropospheric halogen oxidation drives mercury deposition in the Asia Pacific region 
 Asian outflow represents 50% of global anthropogenic mercury emissions, but the atmospheric oxidation pathways controlling its deposition to the adjacent Pacific Ocean remain poorly constrained. Using multi-year snow and atmospheric mercury isotope measurements from Mt. Halla, Jeju Island, Korea, we delineate the mercury sources and oxidation pathways governing deposition to marginal Asia and the western Pacific. Mass-independent fractionation of even-number mercury isotopes (even-MIF; Δ200Hg) correlates with both air mass transport distance and trajectory altitude, indicating the importance of free tropospheric mercury photo-oxidation triggering even-MIF. Coupled anomalies between Δ200Hg and oxygen isotopes of nitrate (Δ17O(NO3-)) in snow indicate that reactive bromine, generated from debromination of local sea salt aerosol, sustains oxidative capacity in the free troposphere and drives active mercury deposition to Mt. Halla snow. Isotope mixing models quantify that halogen-mediated free tropospheric mercury oxidation (68%) exceeds near-surface oxidation (32%). Our results provide field-based evidence for a bromine-driven free tropospheric photo-oxidation mechanism regulating mercury deposition to Asia-Pacific ecosystems.

title: Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS3), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κaa) and the transverse (κab) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κabis extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along thebaxis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation–induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochromecand mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

title: Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in theSTAT2gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti–programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention inSTAT2as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

title: Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain
abstract: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows (Corvus corone) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals
abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°–twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

title: Visualizing symmetry-broken Chern insulators and their quantum melting
abstract: In the presence of a magnetic field, electronic states of moiré quantum materials develop a Hofstadter spectrum that provides a distinctive setting for studying the interplay between band topology and strong electron-electron interaction. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we studied Hofstadter’s states in bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride and directly visualized the formation of interaction-driven symmetry breaking Chern insulators. Our measurements revealed the formation of phases that double, triple, or quadruple the moiré unit cell at fractional filling of the Hofstadter bands as well as states with complex intra–unit cell wave functions. We visualized two distinct quantum phenomena in different Chern states, including quantum melting driven by the appearance and proliferation of topological defects and a quantum transition co-occurring with phase competition and separation.

title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm2. With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm2decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

title: Natural product biosynthesis by guanidine prenyltransferases in plants and bacteria
abstract: Guanidine exists almost exclusively as a resonance-stabilized cation, making its direct enzymatic functionalization challenging. We identified the cyanobacterial enzyme NosH, which catalyzes direct prenyl transfer to free guanidine. Structural and mechanistic analyses revealed guanidine activation by a two-aspartate clamp coupled to prenyl-donor binding through a distinct catalytic architecture. Guided by these features, we identified a large family of guanidine prenyltransferases across bacteria and plants. Plant enzymes produced guanidine alkaloids such as galegine in vitro and heterologous expression of a plant ortholog inNicotiana benthamianaproduced galegine in planta, providing a direct enzymatic link to plant-specialized metabolism.

title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy onNew England Journal of Medicineclinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

title: Noncoding transcription controls the developmental dynamics of long-range gene regulation
abstract: The genomic regions regulating gene expression are often themselves transcribed into a variety of noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs). However, the regulatory roles of this noncoding transcription remain largely unknown. By using live imaging, we reveal that the sequential transcription of ncRNAs emanating from distinct regulatory elements underlies gene activation inDrosophilaembryos. Single-allele covisualization uncovers that optimal gene activation is achieved by only moderate levels of enhancer activity. Disrupting enhancer-associated ncRNAs causes precocious gene activation, providing evidence that ncRNAs control the timing of gene expression in development. We further show that enhancer transcription can regulate long-range interactions within complex regulatory landscapes. We propose that ncRNAs locally modulate regulatory element activity in cis to shape genome organization and orchestrate the temporal control of gene expression in development.

title: Safeguarding global terrestrial vertebrate species from future sea level rise
abstract: Sea level rise (SLR) threatens terrestrial biodiversity, yet its spatiotemporal and species-specific impacts remain unclear. Integrating relative SLR projections across five shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs) with area of habitat (AOH) maps for 34,120 terrestrial vertebrate species, we project that species exposed to SLR will increase from up to 13,680 in 2050 to 15,324 by 2100, including 57 to 63% of birds, 47 to 52% of mammals, 28 to 36% of reptiles, and 20 to 24% of amphibians. In Southeast Asia, inland inundation areas support high richness. Under SSP5-8.5, species facing >10% habitat inundation surge from 18 in 2050 to 109 by 2100, with reptiles and already threatened species overrepresented. Safeguarding SLR refugia—the noninundated habitats for exposed species—is critical, yet more than 96% lie outside protected areas, which means that early international action is required.

title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal
abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd5AlI2, a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd5AlI2gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

abstract: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type–specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.
